newsitem.title: SPAIN: CiU says Bundesbank impressed with Spain - agencies.
newsitem.headline: CiU says Bundesbank impressed with Spain - agencies.

text.p: Spanish Catalan leader Jordi Pujol said on Tuesday the Bundesbank has a very good impression of Spain's economic trend and of its chances to enter European Economic and Monetary Union, according to local news agencies.
No-one at the Madrid headquarters of CiU, or at the regional government in Barcelona, was able to confirm Pujol's remarks.
"The Bundesbank's impression ...of the Spanish economy and Spain's chances to enter Europe, is very good," Pujol told reporters.

"There's a bit of confusion in Europe. There are uncertainties in France, Italy, and other place. But we have to solve our problems which is going well. Everybody recognises that, starting with the Bundesbank's president," he said.
Pujol met with Bundesbank president Hans Tietmeyer on Monday.

Recently, CiU's leader, whose parliamentary group's votes are key to the minority conservative Spanish government, said he would back the government until the exam to enter European economic and monetary Union (EMU) at the beginning of 1998.
